notes.summary: ChatLocale gained required keys in 0.17.0. A hand-written full ChatLocale object no longer compiles and misses texts until it has them. Partial<ChatLocale> overrides are unaffected.
notes.howTo: Add these keys to every full ChatLocale object: approvalTargetLabel, approvalAmbiguousIdWarning, approvalUnknownIdWarning, approvalUnknownIdsWarning. English and German defaults ship with the SDK; the locale and locales props of AiChatProvider take Partial<ChatLocale>, so partial tables need no change. The approval card now names the entity behind every id of a call (approvalSubjects on the provider, default true) and warns for ids without a known name.

notes.summary: A turn stopped at a limit (maxSteps, a budget, totalTimeoutMs) without a final answer now ends with a fixed stop notice instead of the model's last interim sentence. It is English unless the handler's locale is German.
notes.howTo: For a German chat set locale: 'de-DE' on createAiChatHandler, otherwise users get the English notice; other languages replace the texts with budgetStopTexts (DEFAULT_BUDGET_STOP_TEXTS shows the keys). Tests or UI code that expect the model's last sentence after a stop now see the notice as its own text part. The tool-free summary call runs only after a tool limit (maxToolCalls, maxRepeatedFingerprint, maxConsecutiveErrors); such a turn reports finishReason 'tool-calls' with wasTruncated: true in onFinish. Raise limits with createGlirastes({ localLimits }) or the container's limits.

notes.summary: Successful tool results are bounded at maxResultChars (default 16,000). A larger record result becomes an overview with a handle that the new built-in tool read_result reads within the request; read_result counts as a tool call.
notes.howTo: Check tools with large results: the model now sees an overview plus read_result calls, which count against maxToolCalls (default 8). Raise the bound per tool (maxResultChars on the tool, x-glirastes-max-result-chars in OpenAPI) or globally (createAiChatHandler / createGlirastes maxResultChars, container application.maxResultChars), or turn handles off with resultHandles: false to cut results as before. Declare outputDeniedFields (e.g. **.fileUrl for signed URLs) or outputAllowedFields so fields never reach the model or the browser; .glirastes/tools.json output.deniedFields applies app-wide to generated tools.

notes.summary: Earlier tool results in the history keep id and name of every list entry beyond history.maxItems, so follow-ups use real ids. Input tokens per request rise (20 entries: about 645 to 913 tokens per result).
notes.howTo: Nothing to change for the better answers. If input tokens matter more, set history: { keepIdentity: false } on createAiChatHandler to drop further entries with a count as before.

notes.summary: Invalid tool input and guard or budget refusals no longer show 'AI request failed' in the chat but a fixed text (e.g. 'Tool call limit for this turn reached (8).'); the model gets the fields and the reached limit instead of the raw validation dump.
notes.howTo: Update tests, monitors or UI code that match 'AI request failed' for these cases; every other error keeps that text. The turn continues after invalid input as before.

notes.summary: AiChatHandlerConfig.onError is now also called once per failed tool call of a running turn, with a third argument info = { source: 'tool-call', kind: 'denied' | 'invalid-input' | 'failed' }.
notes.howTo: If onError alerts or pages, branch on info?.source === 'tool-call': those calls do not end the turn. Without info the request or the whole turn failed, as before. A throwing onError no longer breaks the stream.

notes.summary: glirastes tools check reports tool-outputs-drift after the upgrade for OpenAPI operations with parameter descriptions or a body-less 204, and when tool-semantics.json has orphaned entries, until glirastes tools refresh.
notes.howTo: Run glirastes tools refresh, review and commit the diff. Connected apps then run glirastes sync and accept the new deployment: until then the signed manifest pins the old schema digests and the changed tools are rejected as E-BINDING-011. Rebuild a runtime container artifact with glirastes-runtime build.

notes.summary: glirastes connect pairs every tool source and stores the key with --dotenv <path>. sync and doctor no longer read .env.local for a non-Next.js app: without --dotenv they read the process environment only.
notes.howTo: In a non-Next.js app pass --dotenv <file> (a Git-ignored, untracked file) to connect, sync, doctor and setup, or set connection.envFile in .glirastes/tools.json, or export GLIRASTES_API_KEY. Do not use --env-file: Node.js reads it itself. Next.js apps keep .env.local.
